intended_object: A procyclic profinite (additive) group: a profinite group G that has an element g whose cyclic subgroup ⟨g⟩ = {n•g : n ∈ ℤ} is dense, i.e. G is topologically generated by one element. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition says there exists g : G with `IsTopologicalGenerator G g`, and `IsTopologicalGenerator` is defined as `DenseRange fun n : ℤ ↦ n • g`. So G is procyclic exactly when the closure of the cyclic subgroup generated by some g is all of G. This is the standard definition (Ribes–Zalesskii, Wilson). The library proves that this is equivalent to `(AddSubgroup.zmultiples g).topologicalClosure = ⊤`, and, on the multiplicative side, to surjectivity of the canonical map from the profinite completion of ℤ. Degenerate cases work: the trivial group is procyclic, as it should be.

On generality: for an arbitrary topological group the same condition is called "monothetic", which is a different notion with a different name. "Procyclic" is by definition a property of profinite groups, so stating it on `ProfiniteAddGrp` is its natural setting. A grep of Mathlib for "monothetic", "procyclic" and "TopologicalGenerator" found no general counterpart. This is the additive version of `ProfiniteGrp.IsProcyclic` in the same file, and it matches it.
